The supplied results on computational political bias do not directly address “computational political bias Wales” specifically, but they do include a Welsh media case study using computational NLP to detect political framing bias in Welsh political news. In particular, one paper tests bias claims about Nation.Cymru’s political reporting by applying a BERT/RoBERTa-based bias detection pipeline and then using an LLM for target-attributed sentiment classification of bias labels, finding measurable differential framing across parties. [1]

More generally, several papers focus on measuring or mitigating political bias in LLMs and news/media systems rather than Wales: they propose evaluation frameworks for “algorithmic partisanship” in LLMs [3], benchmarks for political bias in LLMs across political contexts [5], comparisons between human and model bias detection [4], and fairness/bias issues in news summarization [10]. Another paper proposes inference-time mitigation for adversarially injected political bias in LLM summaries. [2]

Overall, only [1] is directly about Welsh political media; the others cover political bias measurement/mitigation more broadly and are not Wales-specific.
